encounters.cc: Sudden onset of severe abdominal pain and sensation of 'something giving way' 7 days after open cholecystectomy

lines: Sudden onset of severe abdominal pain and sensation of 'something giving way' 7 days after open cholecystectomy
This 67-year-old male with COPD on home oxygen, metastatic lung cancer, and prior DVT presents to the emergency department following recent evaluation for calcium channel blocker-induced edema.
He reports sudden onset of severe abdominal pain and a sensation of "something giving way" in his abdomen 7 days postoperative from an open cholecystectomy.
He states the pain started abruptly after he attempted to lift a heavy object.
- Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) on long-term home oxygen therapy
- Open cholecystectomy (complicated by deep fascial wound dehiscence)
- Albuterol 90 mcg inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for shortness of breath
- Oxygen 2 L/min via nasal cannula continuous
Smoking: Former smoker, 40 pack-year history, quit 1 year ago.
Alcohol: Occasional social use (1-2 drinks per week).
On examination, the patient is afebrile, blood pressure is 130/85 mmHg, heart rate is 110 bpm, and respiratory rate is 22 breaths/min.
His abdomen is distended with a visible bulge at the previous surgical site.
There is no overlying erythema or purulent discharge, but the bulge is tender to palpation and does not reduce with gentle pressure.
- Serum electrolytes are within normal limits
An urgent computed tomography (CT) scan of the abdomen shows protrusion of bowel loops through a defect in the fascial layer of the abdominal wall.

lines: Worsening shortness of breath, productive cough with yellow-green sputum, and inability to sleep lying flat
The patient is a 68-year-old male with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease on long-term home oxygen therapy and metastatic lung cancer who returns six months after his prior COPD exacerbation.
Three days ago, he developed a low-grade fever and fatigue.
Over the past 24 hours, he has become increasingly dyspneic and has been unable to sleep lying flat.
His wife notes that he has been coughing more than usual, with yellow-green sputum.
He is alert but appears exhausted and is using accessory muscles to breathe.
